mainTopic: A wife's כתובה after her husband divides his property; רב הונא's rule that a שכיב מרע's transfer to a fit heir counts as ירושה, and why that matters
overview: First, רב כהנא argues that a wife can collect her כתובה from a deceased daughter's share, since she could collect from any property her husband acquired later. Next, a man split his property between his wife and son but left out one palm tree. רבינא first thinks the wife can collect her כתובה only from that tree. רב יימר replies that if she can collect from the tree at all, she can collect from everything. Then רב הונא rules that when a שכיב מרע writes all his property to someone, a possible heir takes it as ירושה and anyone else takes it as מתנה. רב נחמן objects that this is just רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view, and the two agree that רב הונא meant a dying man who only answered 'To whom else?'. The גמרא asks what difference the label makes, and רבא rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's suggestion about the widow's food support. רבא's answer is that if a fit heir is told 'to you, and after you to so-and-so,' the second person gets nothing, because a ירושה can never be cut off.

steps.title: רב כהנא: She collects from the daughter's share too
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא argues that the wife can collect her כתובה from the deceased daughter's share. She could collect from any property the husband acquired later, so she can collect from this property too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to him: If the husband had later acquired other property, wouldn't she collect her כתובה from it? Since she would collect from newly acquired property, she collects from this share now as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא pushes back on the previous opinion, which held that the wife cannot collect from the deceased daughter's share. He argues that she can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic compares two cases. Property the husband gets later is clearly open to her כתובה. Property that comes back to him, like the dead daughter's share, is no different, so it is also open to her.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to him:
If he had then acquired [other property],
phrases.notes: The husband is the one acquiring. The question is whether his wife could collect her כתובה from new property.

phrases.english: would she not take it?
And since if he had then acquired,
she would take, now too she takes.
phrases.notes: The thing she takes "now" is the share of the daughter who died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: אִילּוּ הָדַר קָנֵי, מִי לָא שָׁקְלָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the previous ruling (from the prior section) that the wife cannot collect from the daughter's share.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the wife cannot collect her כתובה from the deceased daughter's share
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If newly acquired property is open to her, then property that returns to the husband should be open too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She collects her כתובה from the deceased daughter's share.

steps.title: A man leaves out one palm tree; רבינא's first thought
steps.stepSummary: A man divided his property between his wife and son but kept back one palm tree. רבינא first thinks the wife can collect her כתובה only from that tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who divided his property between his wife and his son and kept back one palm tree. רבינא thought she has only that one palm tree for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new real-life case and gives רבינא's first understanding of it. This sets up רב יימר's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, a wife who receives a gift of property together with the children loses her right to collect her כתובה. רבינא thinks the palm tree was left out on purpose, so that she would have something to collect from, but only that tree.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a first idea that may be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: סְבַר רָבִינָא לְמֵימַר means this is only רבינא's first thought. It gets corrected right away, so it is not the final הלכה.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who divided his property
to his wife and his son,
he left over one palm tree.
Ravina thought to say:
She has only the one palm tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case on the same theme of a wife's כתובה after property is divided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First thought: she collects her כתובה only from the palm tree that was left out.

steps.title: רב יימר: Then she shouldn't even get the palm tree
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר challenges רבינא. If she lost her כתובה rights, she should not get even the one palm tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רבינא: If she has no right to collect, then she has no right to the one palm tree either!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר attacks רבינא's middle position. He argues it makes no sense for her rights to stretch only as far as one tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her right to collect a כתובה applies to all of the husband's property together. Either she gave up that right or she didn't. Saying she lost it everywhere except one tree is inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: If she does not have [the right]

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Ravina:
If she does not have [the right to collect],
she does not have the one palm tree either!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרָבִינָא: אִי לֵית לַהּ, חַד דִּיקְלָא נָמֵי לֵית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's first thought from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's view that she collects only from the palm tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her right to collect is all-or-nothing. If it is gone, it is gone from the tree too.

steps.title: Since she collects from the tree, she collects from everything
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר gives the correct ruling. Since she can collect from the palm tree, she can collect her כתובה from all the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since she goes down to collect from the palm tree, she also goes down to collect from all the property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר finishes his point with the opposite conclusion. She did not lose her כתובה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that she clearly can collect from the tree shows that her כתובה rights are still alive. Since those rights cannot be cut down to one tree, she can collect from all of the husband's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (one thing is true, so is the other)

steps.whatToRemember: Leaving out a palm tree does not limit the wife to that tree. It shows she kept her כתובה, so she can collect from everything.

phrases.english: Rather, since she goes down to the palm tree,
phrases.notes: "Goes down" is how the גמרא says she legally steps in to collect from property.

phrases.english: she goes down to all the property as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יימר's challenge with the opposite ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wife collects her כתובה from all of the property, not just the palm tree.

steps.title: רב הונא: Deathbed gift of everything to one person
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that when a שכיב מרע writes all his property to someone, the court checks who the recipient is. If he is fit to inherit, he takes it as ירושה. If not, he takes it as מתנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If a שכיב מרע wrote all his property to someone, we look at who that person is. If he is fit to inherit from him, he takes it as an inheritance. If not, he takes it as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא states a rule about a dying man who writes all his property to one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same document can work in two different ways depending on who receives it. For a possible heir, such as a son, it works as ירושה. For anyone else, it works as a regular מתנה from a dying man.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A person on his deathbed who wrote
all his property to another – we examine;
if he is fit to inherit him –
he takes them as an inheritance,
and if not – he takes them as a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתַב כׇּל נְכָסָיו לְאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic; not connected to the palm tree case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A possible heir takes as ירושה; anyone else takes as מתנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Say openly that you follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects to how רב הונא presented his rule. He says the rule is really the view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, so רב הונא should simply say the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Why are you sneaking this in? If you agree with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, just say "the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה," since your ruling goes according to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן criticizes רב הונא for stating the rule as if it were his own. He points out its real source, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that a person can leave his property as ירושה to whichever heir he chooses. רב הונא's ruling, that an heir takes it as ירושה, depends on that view. So רב נחמן says he should just rule like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה openly.

keyTerms.meaning: To steal stealthily (here: to sneak in a ruling without naming its source)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the rule is wrong. He is objecting to presenting it as a new rule instead of crediting רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Why do you need to sneakily steal?
phrases.notes: He means: why present this rule without saying where it really comes from?

phrases.aramaic: אִי סְבִירָא לָךְ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: If you hold like Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
say: "The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka" –
for your ruling

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הוּא דְּאָזְלָא!
phrases.english: goes according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: גַּנָּבָא גַּנּוֹבֵי לְמָה לָךְ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes how רב הונא presented his rule in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: How רב הונא presented his rule in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule depends on רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view, so it should be stated openly as following him.

steps.title: רב נחמן suggests what case רב הונא meant, and רב הונא agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן suggests that רב הונא's ruling is about a specific case. A dying man was asked, 'Should your property go to so-and-so?' and he answered, 'To whom else?' רב הונא confirms that this is what he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you meant this case: A certain man was dying. People asked him, 'Who should get your property? Maybe so-and-so?' He answered, 'Rather, to whom else?' About this you told us: if that person is fit to inherit him, he takes it as an inheritance, and if not, he takes it as a gift. רב הונא said: Yes, that is what I meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a new reading of רב הונא's ruling so that it is not just a repeat of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רב הונא accepts this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב נחמן complained that רב הונא was simply repeating רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view. Now רב נחמן places the ruling in a different setting. Here the man never wrote a clear document. He only answered a question with 'To whom else?' רב הונא teaches that even this vague answer works: it counts as ירושה if the person is a fit heir, and as מתנה if not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, to whom else? (meaning: of course to him)
Yes, that is what I am saying

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what you are saying:
that there was a certain man who was dying,
and they said to him: to whom should his property go?
phrases.notes: Literally 'his property,' but they are speaking to him, so it means 'your property.'

phrases.english: Perhaps to so-and-so?
And he said to them: Rather, to whom else?
And about this you said to us:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ – נוֹטְלָן מִשּׁוּם יְרוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: If he is fit to inherit him, he takes it as an inheritance,
and if not, he takes it as a gift.
He said to him: Yes, that is what I am saying.
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא answering רב נחמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב נחמן's objection in step 6 by placing רב הונא's ruling in a different, specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was simply repeating רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view about someone who writes his property to one person.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא was talking about a dying man who only answered 'To whom else?' Even such an answer gives the property, as ירושה or as מתנה depending on the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a dying man's casual answer to a question can be enough to transfer his property.

steps.title: What practical difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law depends on whether the person takes the property as ירושה or as מתנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question and sets up the next steps. Either way the person gets the property, so what difference does the label make?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא split the case into ירושה and מתנה. The גמרא now wants a real legal result that depends on that split. The next steps try to answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what law does it matter?
phrases.notes: Since he gets the property either way, why does it matter whether it is called inheritance or gift?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is clear, the גמרא asks what the ירושה/מתנה distinction changes in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical legal result of taking the property as ירושה rather than as מתנה.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה suggests: the widow's food support
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה suggests the difference is the widow's food support. If the person takes it as ירושה, the widow is supported from the property. If he takes it as מתנה, she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה, sitting before רבא, thought to say: If he is fit to inherit him, the dead man's widow is supported from his property. If not, his widow is not supported from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה offers a first answer to the question. He says the label decides whether the widow gets food support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow has the right to be fed from her husband's property while it is with his heirs. רב אדא's idea is that this right applies only when the property passes as ירושה. A מתנה would take it away from her.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava thought
to say, in front of Rava:
If he is fit to inherit him,
his widow is supported from his property,
and if not,
his widow is not supported from his property.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is the widow's food support: she gets it with ירושה but not with מתנה.

steps.title: רבא rejects this: a gift cannot weaken the widow's right
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues with a קל וחומר. If the widow is supported even when the property passes by ירושה, which is a Torah law, she should surely be supported when it passes by a dying man's מתנה, which works only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is her right taken away? Now, with inheritance, which is Torah law, you said his widow is supported from his property. With a gift, which is only rabbinic law, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב אדא's answer. He argues that a מתנה cannot take away the widow's food support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושה is from the Torah, and still the widow keeps her right to food. A dying man's מתנה works only because the רבנן made it work. So it is weaker, and it cannot push the widow aside more than a Torah ירושה does. That means the widow is supported in both cases, and רב אדא's difference falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it weakened / taken away? (said with surprise)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a מתנה is stronger than ירושה. He means that a weaker, rabbinic transfer surely cannot cancel the widow's right, when even the Torah's ירושה does not.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: Is her right lessened?!
phrases.notes: He means: could a gift really cut down the widow's right to food?

phrases.english: Now, with inheritance, which is Torah law,
you said his widow is supported from his property;
with a gift, which is rabbinic law, is it not all the more so?!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that with a מתנה the widow is not supported.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a Torah-level ירושה does not cancel the widow's support, a rabbinic-level deathbed מתנה surely does not.

steps.title: רבא's answer: an inheritance cannot be passed on to a second person
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ruling sent by רב אחא בר רב עויא, following רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. If a man says, 'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,' and the first person is a fit heir, the second person gets nothing. The wording counts as ירושה, and a ירושה cannot be stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the difference is like the ruling רב אחא בר רב עויא sent. According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, if someone says 'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,' and the first person was fit to inherit him, the second person gets nothing in place of the first. This is because the wording is not gift wording but inheritance wording, and an inheritance has no end.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the true practical difference between ירושה and מתנה. A gift can be passed on to a second person afterward, but a ירושה cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a מתנה, the giver can say 'to you, and after you to someone else,' and the second person gets it later. But once the first person is a fit heir, the property comes to him as ירושה. A ירושה stays in his family line, so the giver cannot set up a 'next person.' So the second person gets nothing, and the property goes to the first person's own heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: As he sent (a ruling sent from one place to another)
Has no stopping point; cannot be cut off

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a dying man's property passes as ירושה or as מתנה matters for one main reason. A מתנה can be passed on to a 'next person' ('after you, to so-and-so'), but a ירושה cannot. It keeps going down the heir's own line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רב הונא's ירושה/מתנה split a real practical result. It is the answer to the question of step 8.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִשְׁלַח רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוְיָא:
phrases.english: It is like what Rav Acha bar Rav Avya sent:
According to the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
if one said, 'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,'
if the first person was fit to inherit him,
the second gets nothing in place of the first;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְשׁוֹן מַתָּנָה אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן יְרוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: because this is not gift wording but inheritance wording,
and an inheritance has no stopping point.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, כְּדִשְׁלַח רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב אדא's answer in step 10, רבא gives the correct answer to the question of step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical difference is that with a fit heir the transfer counts as ירושה. A 'next person' named after him gets nothing, because a ירושה cannot be cut off.

steps.title: But the giver himself cut the inheritance off
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: the giver said 'after you, to so-and-so,' so he clearly ended the first person's ירושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: But he cut it off!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a challenge to the ruling from step 11, that the second person gets nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver said, 'after you, to so-and-so.' Those words seem to set an end point for the first person's ownership. So why should the first person's heirs keep everything and the second person get nothing?

keyTerms.meaning: He cut it off, he ended it.
But look! An opening word for a challenge.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
But he cut it off!
phrases.notes: He means the giver himself, who said 'and after you, to so-and-so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 11 that the second person gets nothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that in 'to you, and after you to so-and-so' the second person gets nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The giver clearly set an end to the first person's ownership, so the ירושה should stop there and the property should go to the second person.

steps.title: A ירושה cannot be stopped, whatever the giver thought
steps.stepSummary: The giver thought a ירושה could be stopped, but the Torah says it has no stopping point. So his words 'after you' do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought it has a stopping point, but the Merciful One said it has no stopping point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge. The giver's attempt to stop the ירושה simply does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver chose ירושה wording but then tried to add an end point. The Torah's rule is that a ירושה keeps passing down and cannot be ended. So the giver's mistaken idea cannot change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.

steps.whatToRemember: Once something passes as a ירושה, nobody can set an end point for it. The Torah says a ירושה has no הפסק.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the giver never said 'after you.' He did say it. His words just have no power, because a ירושה cannot be stopped.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the ruling of step 11. The words 'after you, to so-and-so' fail because they try to stop a ירושה, and that is something the Torah does not allow.

phrases.english: He thought it has a stopping point,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the giver, and 'it' is the ירושה.

phrases.english: but the Merciful One said: it has no stopping point.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The giver's intent is overridden by a Torah rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the giver said 'after you, to so-and-so,' his words should end the first person's ירושה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ירושה has no stopping point by Torah law, so the giver's attempt to end it has no effect and the second person gets nothing.
